description:
Our goal is to turn NASA Earth observation data, such as soil moisture, vegetation health and precipitation, into simple, practical insights that help farmers decide what to plant, when to irrigate and how to adapt to a shifting climate.

Who we’re looking for:

Data analysis and visualization

Coding and web development

AI and machine learning

Earth science and agriculture knowledge

Graphic design and storytelling
summary:
Relics: The Space Legacy Atlas is a web app that lets anyone explore the hardware humanity has left beyond Earth. The stories of our rovers, landers and probes are scattered across many archives; Relics brings them into one place.

Users open a 3D solar system and tap a marker on the Moon, on Mars or in deep space to see that object's story: its mission, what it discovered, where it is now, a timeline, images, and the official source behind every fact. The atlas holds 32 verified objects from NASA, ESA, JAXA, ISRO, CNSA and Soviet missions, with live distances for five deep-space probes from NASA/JPL Horizons.

Three Legacy Trails guide learners through connected missions, and three classroom missions give students a task, a notebook and a badge. An AI search answers questions in plain words, using only the verified catalogue and labelling its answers. Anyone can suggest a correction, which moderators review.

These machines are part of human heritage. Relics makes space history easy to find, understand and teach, and shows why objects that fell silent decades ago still matter.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Relics: The Space Legacy Atlas is a free web app about the hardware humanity has left beyond Earth. A 3D solar system shows 32 verified objects as markers: rovers and landers on the Moon and Mars, and probes in deep space. Tapping one opens its profile: mission, operator, dates, status, how sure we are of its location, "Where is it now?", a draggable mission timeline, what it discovered, why it matters, images with credits, and the official source for every fact. Five deep-space probes show live distances from NASA/JPL Horizons.

Users can filter by agency, destination, type, status, decade and scientific field, or move a year slider to see what was in place at any time. Three Legacy Trails (Mars, Lunar, Interstellar) guide learners through connected missions with a badge and a shareable summary. Three Classroom missions give students a task, a notes workspace, AI feedback and a research journal. An AI search answers plain-language questions using only the verified catalogue, with every AI answer labelled. Anyone can suggest a correction, which moderators review.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

These stories are scattered across many archives. Relics puts them in one place for students, teachers, museums and space fans, and shows why machines that fell silent decades ago still matter. We want it to make space history easy to find, understand and teach.

HOW WE BUILT IT

Frontend: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, three.js with React Three Fiber and drei, TanStack Query, React Router. Backend: Node.js and Express, serving the catalogue from JSON files, with a NASA/JPL Horizons client for live positions. AI: Groq API (openai/gpt-oss-20b) with strict output schemas and guardrails. Hosting: Vercel, with Vercel Blob for community contributions. Testing: Node test runner and Playwright browser tests at phone and desktop sizes. No special hardware.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It is not a satellite tracker but a heritage atlas: each object is pinned at its recorded landing coordinates, carries a location-confidence badge (pinned, tracked, projected, approximate, unknown), and links to its sources. The interface opens with an animation that pulls back from Earth to the solar system, uses real planet surface maps, and turns learning into trails and missions.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Accuracy first: no fact without an official source, and the AI may only answer from the catalogue. Accessibility: readable contrast, keyboard use, screen-reader labels, a list equal to the 3D view, and reduced-motion support. It works on phones and without WebGL.
